root_cause.text: The iwcm driver reuses a free list of work_struct objects but maintains a separate per-CM_ID work_list, allowing a work_struct to be freed (returned to free list) and later reused (via INIT_WORK) while still queued in the workqueue, causing list corruption in the workqueue subsystem.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states: "The problem is that a free list of struct iwcm_work is used (for which struct work_struct is embedded), so each call to queue_work() is basically unique and therefore does indeed queue the work. This causes a problem in the work handler which walks the work_list until it's empty to process entries. This means that a single run of the work handler could process item N+1 and release it back to the free list while the actual workqueue entry is still queued. It could then get reused (INIT_WORK...) and lead to list corruption in the workqueue logic." The patch removes the work_list and its associated list operations, and simplifies the work handler to process only the work that triggered it.

candidates.rationale: This call frees the work object back to the free list while the work_struct is still executing in the workqueue. This allows the same work_struct to be reused (via INIT_WORK) before the current handler returns, causing list corruption in the workqueue subsystem.

This queues a work_struct that may have been reused from the free list while the previous instance of that same work_struct is still executing. This violates workqueue atomicity and leads to list corruption.

This adds the reused work to the per-CM_ID work_list. Combined with the premature put_work and subsequent requeue, it enables a scenario where a work_struct still in execution is re-added to a list and requeued.

This removes the work from the work_list before it is freed by put_work. While necessary for correct processing, it occurs before the work_struct has completed execution, allowing the freed work to be reused prematurely.

This loop triggers the sequential processing of events on the work_list. It is the point where work items are removed, freed, and then later potentially requeued, creating the window for the use-after-free / double-queue race.

Author: Bart Van Assche <bvanassche@acm.org>
Date:   Wed Jun 5 08:50:59 2024 -0600

    RDMA/iwcm: Simplify cm_event_handler()
    
    queue_work() can test efficiently whether or not work is pending. Hence,
    simplify cm_event_handler() by always calling queue_work() instead of only
    if the list with pending work is empty.
    
    Signed-off-by: Bart Van Assche <bvanassche@acm.org>
    Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20240605145117.397751-4
bic_trace_step.reason: The commit changes cm_event_handler to always call queue_work() instead of conditionally. The vulnerable construct described in the root cause (reuse of a work_struct from a free list while still queued in the workqueue) is not present in this function. The function only adds work to a list and queues it; it does not manage the freeing or reinitialization of work_struct objects. Therefore, the function does not contain the vulnerable construct.

bic_trace_step.reason: In cm_work_handler (around line 870-880), after removing a work item from work_list, the function calls put_work(work) to return it to the free list while still holding the work pointer and later uses work->event. Since put_work adds the work to cm_id_priv->work_free_list, another thread in cm_event_handler can get the same work via get_work, call INIT_WORK on it, and queue_work while the original handler is still running. This causes the work_struct to be reused while still potentially referenced by the workqueue, leading to list corruption. This is the vulnerability described in the root cause. No fix is present in this initial commit.
